title: Academics
intro: Two respected pathways on one campus in Kisakasaka: the NECTA Tanzanian national curriculum (Grades 1–6) and our Cambridge Assessment International Education Wing (Years 1–6), built on a joyful Pre-Primary foundation.

levels.name: Baby Class & Nursery
levels.summary: Play-based early childhood learning where every child builds confidence in phonics, early numeracy, social sharing, and bilingual communication.
highlights: Two caring educators in every room, maximum 18 children
Daily phonics, storytelling, and hands-on number sense
Shaded outdoor play, creative arts, and a structured rest hour
English and Swahili spoken warmly throughout the day
Breakfast, hot lunch, and daily Madrasa / moral stories included

levels.name: NECTA Primary Wing
levels.summary: The Tanzanian national curriculum taught in English with strong Swahili mastery, small classes, weekly laboratory science, and thorough preparation for national assessments.
highlights: Capped at 24 pupils per class for personal attention
Daily 30-minute guided reading and library borrowing
Practical science and computer lessons from Grade 1
All stationery, breakfast, hot lunch, and Madrasa included in fees
Termly parent-teacher conferences with clear written targets

levels.name: Cambridge International Wing
levels.summary: Our Cambridge Assessment International Education stream develops inquiry, critical thinking, and global fluency across Lower and Upper Primary (Years 1–3 and Years 4–6).
highlights: Official Cambridge Primary progression from Year 1 to Year 6
Inquiry-led Science and Mathematics in dedicated labs
Global Perspectives, Art & Design, and strong English literacy
Seamless international benchmark for globally mobile and local families
Includes full stationery pack, daily breakfast & lunch, and Madrasa

levels.name: Madrasa, Languages & Leadership
levels.ages: All Classes · Baby Class to Year 6
levels.summary: Rooted in Zanzibari heritage and global citizenship: daily Madrasa and character education alongside English, Kiswahili, and Arabic fluency.
highlights: Daily timetabled Madrasa and moral reflection included in the fee structure
Trilingual exposure: English medium with strong Kiswahili and Arabic
Weekly assembly speaking roles so every child learns to address an audience
Nutritious school breakfast and hot lunch served fresh every day
Safe, inclusive environment with a full-time pastoral care officer

enrichment.title: Clubs, games and leadership
enrichment.text: Every learner joins afternoon clubs and sports alongside their classroom studies, discovering talents in technology, arts, athletics, and leadership.

items.title: Robotics & Coding
items.text: Block-based coding, Scratch, and hands-on STEM kits in our 34-workstation computer lab.

items.title: Debate & Public Speaking
items.text: Weekly assembly showcases and junior debate circles in English and Kiswahili.

items.title: Arts, Ngoma & Choir
items.text: Drawing, painting, traditional percussion ensemble, and Culture Day performances.

items.title: Football, Netball & Athletics
items.text: House competitions, physical education, and annual Sports Day on the Kisakasaka field.

items.title: Swimming & Water Safety
items.text: Structured learn-to-swim sessions and water confidence for primary classes.

items.title: Environment & Global Perspectives
items.text: School kitchen garden, recycling projects, and community care around Kisakasaka.

items.title: Media & Storytelling
items.text: Junior photography, school newsletter writing, and creative visual projects.

items.title: Reading & Writers Club
items.text: 640 library titles, daily reading logs, and our annual bilingual story anthology.

results.title: Academic standards, honestly reported
results.note: We track every child's literacy, numeracy, and science mastery across both our NECTA and Cambridge Primary wings.

dayInLife.text: Gates open; school buses arrive; teachers welcome pupils at the courtyard.
Morning assembly, national anthem, and reflection of the day.
Morning core lessons (English, Mathematics, Science) with school breakfast break at 09:45.
Hot nutritious lunch from the school kitchen, rest, and library reading corner.
Afternoon lessons: Humanities, ICT/Lab practicals, Art & Design, and daily Madrasa.
Clubs, games, and guided homework support on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
School buses depart Kisakasaka campus; parent pick-up at the visitor bay.

points.title: Assessment for learning
points.text: Every unit starts with a short diagnostic and ends with a written target shared with parents. No surprises at the end of term.

points.title: Language with purpose
points.text: English for academic fluency across NECTA and Cambridge streams, Swahili for national pride, and Arabic in Madrasa.

points.title: Stationery & meals provided
points.text: Every child receives the same high-quality books, stationery, breakfast, and lunch at school — ready to focus on learning.

points.title: Reporting every learner by name
points.text: Class teachers review each pupil's progress every half term and invite parents in early whenever extra support is needed.
